text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN
- The government issued a notification declaring Friday as a half-holiday and Sunday as the weekly holiday.
- The State (central) Bank of Pakistan has spelled out the foreign exchange mobilisation programme announced by Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif to relieve the country of foreign debts.

- Three state-run banks have received $1.3 million in the last few days after Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif's call to donate foreign exchange and open foreign currency fixed-deposit accounts for two years.
- Japan is expected to offer $500 million to Pakistan shortly to undertake four major development projects.
- Motor dealers have urged the government to allow import of reconditioned cars which will provide five billion rupees to the exchequer in terms of customs duties.
- Gunmen killed a senior official of the Punjab provincial government in Lahore.

- Former prime minister Benazir Bhutto's Pakistan People's Party (PPP) will sue the Sunday Times for carrying what a PPP spokesman in Islamabad called a "concocted and baseless story" implicating her husband Asif Zardari in drug smuggling.
BUSINESS RECORDER

- The tax collection target has been curtailed to 334 billion rupees from 340.9 billion with the new government committed to stay within four percent budget deficit limit by mobilising non-tax revenue and squeezing current spending.
- The government requested the International Monetary Fund to send a review mission to Pakistan as early as possible.
FINANCIAL POST
- The government is putting the final touches to a new export policy which is to be announced shortly.
THE NEWS

- Former army chief General Aslam Beg told the Supreme Court the former Inter-Services Intelligence chief had arranged to distribute 140 million rupees, deposited by former Mehran Bank chief Younis Habib, among politicians in the 1990 elections.
- Delegates from Pakistan, India, China and the United States holding unofficial talks in Islamabad expressed concern over India's latest Prithvi missile test.
- Banks are offering 7.5 to 9.0 percent on foreign currency deposits under Prime Minister's programme for debt retirement.
- The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Resources is about to cancel an agreement to build a $120 million Indus Pipeline project from Port Qasim to Jamshoro thermal power plant.
- The Karachi Stock Exchange said it had contributed 10 million rupees to the Prime Minister's Debt Repayment Fund.
-- Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
